submission.justification:
Simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c (100k events each): R1 peaks near 3 cm at 4.70 sigma (2 cm: 4.34, 4 cm: 4.22, 1 cm: 4.13, 6 cm: 3.42). R3 reaches 3.73 sigma at 3 cm and 2.89 at 6 cm; R2 reaches 2.91 at 3 cm and 2.13 at 6 cm. R1 at 3 cm gives the best separation of the three candidates. Lifetime: the documents include no quantitative aging data for any radiator. The only relevant hints are that R3 carries a hydrophobic treatment (suggesting porous radiators are moisture-sensitive) and that the gas volume is flushed with dry nitrogen, which should limit humidity exposure. R1 is therefore acceptable on the available evidence, but its lifetime stability is not verified and should be confirmed (e.g., humidity-aging test) before procurement. The 6 cm result is worse than 3 cm, so the thickness should not be increased. Thickness is 3 cm, within the 1–6 cm range.</justification>
